signal_watch.author: Vercel AI
signal_watch.summary: Vercel Agent can now investigate alerts from Vercel monitors before they reach your paging system. With validation enabled for a webhook destination, only alerts Agent classifies as Critical are sent to it. To enable validation: Open a monitor’s notification settings and create or link a webhook destination for your paging system, such as incident.io. Select Critical Only next to that destination. You can also configure notification destinations with the Vercel CLI using verc

signal_watch.title: Vercel Sandbox commands now support stdin
signal_watch.author: Vercel AI
signal_watch.summary: Vercel Sandbox now lets you send input to running commands through standard input (stdin). Use it to exchange messages with stdio MCP servers such as agent-browser , or send data to other command-line programs while they run. In the TypeScript SDK, set stdin: true and detached: true in runCommand() . Use writeStdin() to send input and closeStdin() when you’re done: You can also set stdin to a Node.js readable stream, such as process.stdin . The SDK forwards the stream’s data

hot_rank.author: Vercel AI
hot_rank.summary: Vercel Agent can now investigate alerts from Vercel monitors before they reach your paging system. With validation enabled for a webhook destination, only alerts Agent classifies as Critical are sent to it. To enable validation: Open a monitor’s notification settings and create or link a webhook destination for your paging system, such as incident.io. Select Critical Only next to that destination. You can also configure notification destinations with the Vercel CLI using verc

hot_rank.title: Vercel Sandbox commands now support stdin
hot_rank.author: Vercel AI
hot_rank.summary: Vercel Sandbox now lets you send input to running commands through standard input (stdin). Use it to exchange messages with stdio MCP servers such as agent-browser , or send data to other command-line programs while they run. In the TypeScript SDK, set stdin: true and detached: true in runCommand() . Use writeStdin() to send input and closeStdin() when you’re done: You can also set stdin to a Node.js readable stream, such as process.stdin . The SDK forwards the stream’s data
